questions.question:
Three particles \(P,Q\) and \(R\) are moving along the vectors \(\overrightarrow A=\hat i+\hat j,~~\overrightarrow B=\hat j+\hat k\) and \(\overrightarrow C=-\hat i+\hat j\) respectively. They strike on point and start to move in different directions. Now particle \(P\) is moving normally to the plane which contains vector \(\overrightarrow A\) and \(\overrightarrow B.\) Similarly particle \(Q\) is moving normally to the plane that contains the vector \(\overrightarrow A\) and \(\overrightarrow C.\)The angle between the direction of motion of \(P\) and \(Q\) is:
1.\(\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\)2.\(\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\)
3.\(\cos^{-1}\left({\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}}\right)\)4.\(\cos^{-1}\left(\sqrt{{3}}\right)\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(\overrightarrow A.\overrightarrow B= AB\cos\theta\) Step:Find the angle between the directions of motion of\(P\)and\(Q.\) Given,\(\vec A =\hat i+\hat j,~\vec B=\hat j+\hat k, ~\vec C=-\hat i+\hat j \) Since particle\(P \)moves normal to the plane containing\(\vec A \)and\(\vec B,\) \(\vec P=\vec A\times \vec B= \begin{vmatrix} \hat i &\hat j & \hat k\\ 1&1&0\\ 0&1&1 \end{vmatrix} =\hat i-\hat j+\hat k\) Similarly, particle \(Q\) moves normal to the plane containing\(\vec A\)and \(\vec C,\) \(\vec Q=\vec A\times \vec C= \begin{vmatrix} \hat i &\hat j & \hat k\\ 1&1&0\\ -1&1&0 \end{vmatrix} =2\hat k\) Now,\(\vec P.\vec Q=(1)(0)+(-1)(0)+(1)(2)=2\) Also,\(|\vec P|=\sqrt{1^2+(-1)^2+1^2} =\sqrt 3,~~|\vec Q|=2 \) Then,\(\cos\theta=\dfrac{\vec P. \vec Q}{|\vec P||\vec Q|}=\dfrac{2}{2\sqrt 3}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt 3}\) Therefore,\(\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt 3}\right) \) Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

1. \(90^\circ\)
2. \(60^\circ\)
3. \(45^\circ\)
4. \(30^\circ\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(\cos \theta=\dfrac{\overrightarrow A.\overrightarrow B}{|\overrightarrow A||\overrightarrow B|}\) Step:Find the angle between\(\overrightarrow{F}\)and\(\overrightarrow{P}\). Given:\(\overrightarrow{P}=\sin (k t) \hat{i}\text-\cos( k t )\hat{j}\) We know that; \(\overrightarrow {F}= \dfrac{d\overrightarrow {P}}{dt}\) \(\Rightarrow \overrightarrow {F}= k \cos (kt)\hat i + k\sin(kt)\hat j\) The dot product of the vectors\(\overrightarrow{F}\)and\(\overrightarrow{P}\)is given by; \(\overrightarrow{F}\cdot \overrightarrow{P} = k(\cos(kt)\hat i+ \sin(kt)\hat j)\cdot (\sin (k t) \hat{i}\text-\cos( k t )\hat{j})\) \(\Rightarrow \overrightarrow{F}\cdot \overrightarrow{P} = k(\cos(kt)\sin(kt)- \sin(kt)\cos( k t ))=0\) \(\Rightarrow \overrightarrow{F}\cdot \overrightarrow{P} =0\) So, the vectors \(\vec P\) and \(\vec F\) are perpendicular. Therefore, theangle between\(\overrightarrow{F}\)and\(\overrightarrow{P}\)is \(90^{\circ}.\) Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.
